payload.summary: All three amendments identify genuine technical defects. fr-7-f0d55cc5 correctly flags partial mutation before validation completion in enforce_invariants, with tests that only pass due to a fragile assumption about default state. fr-7-6c8fdcb3 identifies a real mass-accounting inconsistency where reserve_g is documented as the growth/reproduction fund but is never debited for hatching or maturation, making it a dead-end pool. fr-7-baf66be2 correctly identifies that the budget guard is disabled wholesale by any action flux rather than subtracting known action deltas from the residual, masking unrelated leaks in mixed ticks.

votes.rationale: Verified: enforce_invariants clamps DO, pH, and 40+ indices on &mut TankState before reaching later validation checks (check_unit_interval, check_non_negative for reserve_g, etc.). If a later check returns Err, earlier clamps have already mutated state. The validation.rs tests (lines 92-127) assert engine.full_state() == &expected after error, which holds only because TankState::new() produces values already within all clamp ranges. This is a real fragile-assumption bug: any future change to defaults, or any test that constructs state with out-of-range clampable values plus a failing later check, will break the state-equality invariant. The proposed fixes (reorder validation before clamping, or remove the fragile assertions) are both sound.

Verified: reserve_g is documented as 'the retained share of feeding that has not yet been used for growth/reproduction' and is populated by route_consumed_food (assimilated * growth_frac). However, fund_live_shrimp_biomass_from_water (used by both hatching at line 443 and maturation at line 530) pulls exclusively from dissolved water pools (DON, TAN for nitrogen; DOC, DIC for carbon) and never touches reserve_g. reserve_g is only decremented during mortality (transferred to detritus), making it an ever-accumulating dead-end pool. This contradicts the documented routing contract and creates a mass accounting inconsistency where the explicit 'growth/reproduction' fund is never spent on growth or reproduction. The amendment's proposed fix—debiting reserve_g first, then falling back to water pools if needed—correctly aligns the implementation with the documented model.

Verified: tick_has_closed_system_nitrogen/carbon (lines 563-575) return false (disabling the guard entirely) whenever ANY of the 5 action labels (feed, water_change, siphon_detritus, add_shrimp, remove_shrimp) has non-zero flux. This means a tick with a legitimate water_change AND an unrelated nitrogen leak from a bug elsewhere will never trigger BudgetImbalance—the action flux masks the entire tick. The code already demonstrates the correct pattern for chemistry carbon (lines 577-589): carbon_guard_delta_mg subtracts the known chemistry_external_carbon_flux_mg from the net delta, then checks the residual. Applying this same residual-based subtraction to action fluxes would allow mixed ticks to still detect unexplained drift while correctly accounting for known open-system exchanges.
